summary: Keyflower is a clever hybrid of worker placement and auction where you bid workers to win tiles, then use those same (or other) workers to activate tiles for resources and points, including tiles in opponents' villages. The tension between using workers now versus saving them for the endgame winter bidding round is the heart of the game, and building an efficient engine across four rounds feels very satisfying.
praised: Clever double-use of workers for both bidding and activating tiles
High interaction via using resources/skills on opponents' tiles
Satisfying variable setup and modular board every game
Rewards planning and engine-building without excessive downtime
Strong tension around the winter round using only your held tiles
criticised: Can suffer from significant analysis paralysis, especially at higher player counts
Rules and icons have a learning curve for new players
Some randomness in which tiles come up for auction
Can feel like a 'take that' game to newer players unfamiliar with the shared-tile mechanic
Endgame scoring tiles can create swingy, hard-to-predict outcomes

interaction.kind: auction/bidding plus using workers on others' tiles

scoring.why: points come from a mix of resources, skills, workers, and building combinations set by winter tiles, so the winning strategy varies each game
